![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14201311/assets/9674072fe2d9f831635dfd2994b97ea6e9603dd576586f80e4b1b2e6a2373564.png)

The graph above shows the relationship between $x$ and $y.$ Given that $y$ is inversely proportional to $x,$ find the value of $a.$
question.worked_solution:
Since $y$ varies inversely with $x,$ we use the equation

$$
y=\frac{k}{x}.
$$

In the graph, we notice a point with $y=\frac{1}{2}$ and $x=5.$ We substitute this data into the equation to find $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & =\frac{k}{5} \\ \frac{1}{2}\cdot 5 & =k \\ \frac{5}{2} & =k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse variation equation that relates $y$ and $x$ is

$$
y=\frac{(\frac{5}{2})}{x}=\frac{5}{2x}.
$$

From the graph, we also have that $y=\frac{5}{2}$ when $x=a.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{2} & =\frac{5}{2a} \\ 10a & =10 \\ a & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
